{{short description|Belgian applied mathematician}}
'''Christine De Mol''' (born 23 April 1954){{r|cv}} is a Belgian applied mathematician and mathematical physicist interested in [[inverse problem]]s, [[Regularization (mathematics)|regularization]], [[wavelet]]s, and [[machine learning]], and known for her work on [[proximal gradient method]]s and the application of [[proximal gradient methods for learning]].  She is a professor of mathematics at the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]], and the former chair of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] Activity Group on Imaging Science.

==Education==
De Mol was educated at the Université libre de Bruxelles, earning a [[Licentiate (degree)|licence]] in physics in 1975 and a Ph.D. in 1979, with a dissertation ''Sur la régularisation des problèmes inverses linéaires''{{r|cv}}
under the joint supervision of Jean Reignier and Mario Bertero.{{r|mg}}

==Career==
De Mol became a researcher for the Belgian [[National Fund for Scientific Research]] (FNRS), obtaining a permanent position there in 1981 and becoming a director of research in 1996. Meanwhile, she had obtained a [[habilitation]] from the Université libre de Bruxelles; her habilitation thesis was ''Super-résolution en microscopie confocale''. In 1998 she gave up her position with the FNRS, becoming an honorary researcher with them, to become a full professor at the Université libre de Bruxelles. She was head of the mathematics department at the university for 2009–2010,{{r|cv}} and chair of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] Activity Group on Imaging Science for 2012–2013.{{r|siagis}}
